question: In the 50-year study of British doctors, how much life did lifelong smokers lose on average?
answer: About 10 years. Doctors who smoked all their lives died about a decade earlier than those who never smoked. Stopping at 30 won back nearly all of it; stopping at 50, about six years; even at 60, about three. Everyone knows a smoker who reached 90; the study counted all the others too.
move: The one exception you remember hides the many you never met.
ask: Which risky habit do I excuse because I know one person it never seemed to hurt?
trap: About 2 years, since everyone knows a smoker who reached 90.
reference: Doll, Peto, Boreham & Sutherland, Mortality in relation to smoking: 50 years' observations on male British doctors, BMJ, 2004
